messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: high error rate + latency on continuous-batcher-prod-us-east. 5xx spike, multiple containers restarting. Auto-detected OOMs and CUDA faults.

maya: Seeing continuous-batcher queue grow on pool `cb-us-east-07`. GPU mem climbs -> OOM -> container restart loop. CUDA error in logs: `cudaGetDevice() -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. 10 restarts in last 4m.

sanjay: Pasting tail of runtime log from one pod: 
```
I0315 03:12:14.123 runtime.cc:421] BatchAccumulator size=1372
E0315 03:12:15.456 gpu_worker.cc:87] Fatal: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at step 1024
E0315 03:12:15.457 runtime.cc:489] terminating abnormally: Device-side memory access
```

ryan: Confirming same across 6 pods. CPU fine but GPU stuck with high mem alloc. I pushed a temporary k8s patch to reduce prefetch and prefer small-batch mode: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher PREFETCH_WINDOW=1 BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=128 -n runtime
kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher -n runtime
```

eli: I'm cordoning the worst nodes so scheduler moves new pods elsewhere. Doing drain on `gpu-node-07` and `gpu-node-08` now.

deploy-bot: Patch applied at 03:16 UTC by ryan. Rollout: 6/12 pods updated.

customer-support: We have incoming CS alerts: Acme Corp (prod) and BetaChat report timeouts ~03:10-03:20 UTC, about ~15% of requests failing with 503s. Raising severity to P1 customer-impact.

maya: Quick mitigation succesful? After PREFETCH_WINDOW=1 the queue growth stopped on updated pods, GPU mem stabilized on those. Remaining older pods still OOMing. Suggest rollback of recent aggressive prefetch PR (#4121) that landed yesterday.

sanjay: I can trigger a targeted rollout to replace pods still on the old image and also patch the prefetch env across the cluster. Also seeing `BatchAggregator` growth when request shapes are tiny but many in parallel — code path allows unbounded accumulation if prefetch and accumulator are both enabled. Repro locally with load test.

ryan: Started rolling replace of pods on nodes that flapped. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher -n runtime --timeout=10m` and monitoring. Also added temporary healthcheck backoff to reduce re-tries.

eli: Drains complete for 07/08, new pods scheduled on healthy nodes. Some nodes show residual page faults; kernel logs indicate GPU page fault storms -> driver resets. We're isolating those nodes.

maya: Enabled fallback routing to stable model variant on region `us-east-2` for heavy customers (Acme Corp). Command: `redwoodctl routes set --customer acme --model tundra-v1 --region us-east-2`. This reduces load to the flaky pool.

kate: Summary for handoff: root cause likely regression in aggressive prefetch + accumulator interaction causing unbounded batch growth -> GPU OOMs -> container crashes -> node flaps. Customer impact: multiple customers experienced timeouts, elevated 5xx. Mitigations applied: lowered PREFETCH_WINDOW, rolled replace of pods, cordoned bad nodes, enabled regional fallback for affected customers.

nina: (added) I'll take night oncall. Plan: finish rollout, revert PR #4121 in staging and run the load reproduction test overnight, gather coredumps from affected pods, and prepare a postmortem doc.

maya: One more: collected core + nvcrash dumps uploaded to s3 `s3://redwood-debug/3421000000/`. Permission granted to oncall and infra team.

sanjay: Next steps: revert aggressive prefetch in canary, add a hard cap on BatchAccumulator entries, add metric + alert for accumulator depth > 1000, and update runbook to include `PREFETCH_WINDOW` knob for emergency.

kate: Handoff note to @nina at 04:00 UTC. Please coordinate w/ support for customer follow-ups and schedule incident review tomorrow. :thumbsup:

nina: Acknowledged. Will run the staging replay, collect traces, and propose mitigations (code + config) by 09:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident marked acked by oncall at 03:40 UTC. Follow-up ticket: #INC-3421000000 created for postmortem.
